Content: City streets run for only 5 to 10 blocks. All other used to be streets are now small farm gardens hugging a bike path.

There would be more equitable access to land and resources. Roads would be windy and slower. There would be many farm stands. It would be common for things to be given away, and mutuality would run on the honor system. Sharing is a primary value for our abundance and wellbeing.
Railroads can be heard and seen.

Development is dense. We carve out civilization around and with water. There are community hubs where people are accessing public goods – giving and receiving – constant flow of activity and people. Soft whirl of trains in flow.
Where structures are transformed into domes - purpose is found from Creator.
Nature is healthy and prioritized, including in how cities use /zone their land.

There are park centers where people can gather for meals, connection, and helping each other out. People practice multiple healing and spirit pathways in the same communities and spaces. People depend on each other instead of being so isolated or independent.
Every neighborhood has a "hub" that includes garden space, a community kitchen, and a gathering space. It's used for celebrations and sharing.
Kanata - our strength is in the village. The village is our strength.

The yellow & red rose bush in front of ancestor Mimi’s house is full, blossoming in June, trimmed and cleaned in the winter.  Jonah’s group home has turned into a thriving home for other young adults with special needs.  Juniper and Olive’s great grand children sit in the front yard of what once was their private home but is now a shared front yard for the whole neighborhood to play in.  The zipline that was put up in 2000 during covid is now back for all the children in the neighborhood.  The terraced garden that their ancestors planted is now tended to by neighbors on a rotating cycle and providing food for the surrounding neighborhood.  The coveted hot tub for 3 has been replaced by a hot tub for 10.  The neighbors have the code and come and go to enjoy.  The garage that was turned into a home is now a community use center that neighbors use for meditation, hosting community gatherings, and of course… access to the hot tub.

There are quiet spaces that people hold and tend to as sacred spaces.  Some of them are places of spirit practice, some of them are simply decorated rooms.  They all have the simple markers of life.  A few flowers.  Tea.  Incense.  Earth.  Art.  Loneliness is not very common.  Meals, neighborhoods, work, healthcare, education are all so communal and involved that communities have oriented more toward making sure there are quiet spaces for people to practice and be.

Each community is formed as a result of thoughtful consideration of what is needed for a place to thrive and the beings in it. We know that we need food and so we need someone who knows how to grow food, and build greenhouses depending on the climate. People need to live in structures so there are people who know how to design and build and manufacture the materials for each. We have people who are skilled at trading fairly with neighboring communities for their specialties. Everyone is skilled in communicating with the land, the water, the numerous relatives that inhabit a place with the humans. Humans speak their languages and know when they are in consent with our plans and when they aren’t. Humans know to consult nature before any planning takes place.

Accessibility of green spaces. The development and design of cities and communities are centered around people, not money. Using infrastructure to benefit people, as opposed to the real estate developers. For the benefit of people and not to sell people something.

Date/Circle Name: 2/1/25 St Louis Park, MN BIPOC The Coven
Content: There are smaller neighborhoods and communities, with a common inner place where people learn, share, exchange. More time to love, nourish and raise children in smaller groups. Instead of classrooms there is experiential learning. Learning intergenerationally, out in community.

Date/Circle Name: 2/1/25 St Louis Park, MN BIPOC The Coven
Content: People sustain themselves off the grid and are not dependent upon governments.
Shrines & altars dot the landscape, feeding holy beings of all lineages.
Jails and prisons from the present day still stand as reminders of the past.
Doors are open on the streets.  People interact and are welcome.  You see people of every shade connecting to sort out the questions of the day – and to have fun.  You hear laughter all around.
Prisons are already gone.  Crime will be more interpersonal and around family dynamics and differences of opinion.  We will be focused on building emotional awareness, somatic connection, etc.

A building needs to be repurposed. New buildings are made from reclaimed wood. Climatic tracking is part of the smart building and it is a spiritual practice to track what is happening in climate for the good of all.

Building covered in greenery. Urbanness being one with nature. Animal hospital - mom elephant taking baby elephant to hospital. Nature is one with us, no fear. We bring back some extinct species. Horizon going into sunset on the beach.

Neighborhoods choose hours when AI is in use…and hours when humanity is practiced in different ways.   Neighborhoods sound like passionate conversations, laughter.  They smell of food cooked for shared meals-spices and sweetness.  Of gardens freshly tilled.  You see laundry hanging on shared clothesline as people share tasks and appliances.
In the city scape, the potholes have been cultivated as gardens.  They are lush, vibrant, growing, and everywhere.

There are neighbors who get together to pick up any trash, prune plants, fix things around the neighborhood, and they complete all their work quickly and efficiently because so many neighbors come out to help.
There are no uneven sidewalks, there are no cracks in the sidewalk, and no one has trouble ambulating on the sidewalks because they are wide, clear, and accessible.
Everyone has a balcony or small outdoor/green space they can enjoy. The parks are well-maintained and are constantly being improved.
Buildings in NYC are covered in green and the Hudson River is full of life. People have slowed down.

There are less humans in the world, by choice, not by war. We need less buildings, so we build less buildings. More pre-existing buildings are all repaired with preexisting materials from other structures.
There are no landfills

There would be buildings and infrastructure designed to be in balance with the environment.  Engineers of balance would study for years – math, physics, and applied relationship to land, water, and beings.

Libraries become banks that store the memories and histories of a place. Libraries help us remember a time when technology was extractive, a reminder of what we don’t want to return to. Libraries are also the place people go to in order to access necessary tools that can be shared. Like the young kid who goes to the local library to check out kites to take to the local park for that windy day in the fall.
It feels like this… https://photos.app.goo.gl/C8yv2QgmZYR7GmrM7
It smells like the forest, even in our “urban” areas
Cities were re-organized to re-open migratory trails and corridors, like how dams are being torn down to re-open running rivers

The city is colorful and vibrant with people everywhere. There are central plazas and the idea of “business downtowns” are replaced with public goods (libraries / art spaces / community gathering centers). The city is enshrined with nature, blending habitats with the natural earth around us. Animals are frequently roaming, but people don’t mind them. What were once borders are as casual and mundane as crossing to another city.

Date/Circle Name: 2/27/25 Redwood City and North Fair Oaks, CA Sobrato 2
Content: So many buildings are empty now.  Other people migrate into homes that are left well stocked – even with gifts for the next people who will move in.

Date/Circle Name: 2/27/25 Redwood City and North Fair Oaks, CA Sobrato 2
Content: Fruit trees line the streets, and everyone helps tend to them…and benefits from them.  The roads no longer have cars.  They have laughter, safety, trust, trikes, mentorship.  No one feels alone or left out.
The alleys feel warm and welcoming.
Empty buildings are vibrant with the green life that grows through it.
Roofs have gardens.  Gardeners are abundant and valued.
Back yards are connected playgrounds that bring everyone together.

Blue skies, green grass.  Houses are small.  We learned a while back that thriving is actually downsizing – simplifying.  Everyone has a home.  There aren’t any huge immaculate homes anymore.  There are community buildings where meals are prepared.  People eat together very often.  There are gardens where the food is grown.  Roads aren’t roads any more.  For the most part, most transportation is as far as you can get with your own feet.  The rest is more communal.
We have green spaces everywhere.
We live as a village.  People take care of one another’s kids.  Cook for one another.  There are town and community spaces.

Crawfordsville is still cradled in forest.  All of the old flat buildings have gardens on them.  There are solar panels built into the old spaces.  All efficiently engineered.  That window over there is where kids play music with the windows open.  That street is all green area, now.  AI is helpful.
The 2nd and 3rd floors of buildings have been converted into good housing space.  Teaching space.  Care space.
As things burned down or crumbled – green space emerged…any new building building is now very efficient and built for specific needs.
There is lots of space for people to gather.  150 years ago, the first communal space was secured where the community truly prioritized access for everyone.

People live more closely in communities and colonies that are very much more integrated with nature.  Technology is useful, but there is a frugalness to it.  We don’t rely on it–it is useful.  People will be highly sensitive to themselves, nature, the environment.  We are in treehouses, and other buildings that are literally on the border.

Houses are built in concentric circles. People’s dwellings are in a circle and they share a courtyard in the center when children play. They’ll play badminton outside until it’s too dark to see the birdie. Aunts and uncles will tell jokes about what they encounter in other villages. They bring goods back to the Center of the village and cook in washing basins and in the earth.
We build healing temples instead of prisons. We build art studios.  Our bodies, individually and collectively are the temples.
Buildings would look interesting…beautiful and curvy.  Self sustaining in terms of energy.  People would move more slowly, because the roads would no longer be straight.

Spaces for person to person and being to being connection. Outside of technology. Face to face. Heart to heart. Spaces where food is shared and eaten together for example. Where each individual shares the responsibility of holding and creating space as well as participating in the space. Equal power among people.
There are no prisons, resources are funneled to communities to heal, nurture and rebuild.
The carceral system becomes obsolete because the community cares for every person as a whole and all their needs, health, food, shelter.

My vision is multigenerational, multiple families sharing space. Neighborhoods and homes are designed and made of clay, round in structure. People live in multiple small pods, families, sharing land, sharing space, food is everywhere, full of joy, with people interacting.

There are less options about where we live.

We live in small communities and pods. We share labor and child raising. We depend on one another and there is reverence for reciprocity. There is no glorifying or worshipping individualism or consumerism.

Library- renewal. Family visits library. Kids step away to get seeds from the seed bank. One of the parents step away to check out translation device in prep for community meeting. Other parents get cloth/material from reserve of used clothing to re-use. There are books, classes, exchanges of wisdom happening in various ways with multiple items, through lots of avenues.

Libraries are deeply valued. Plants everywhere. Tech abilities, creating microgrids distributed among communities. We return to old ways of textile production. We welcome and make space for people from other places.
We have global citizenship, but pride ourselves on caring for our neighborhoods and communities.
Small pastoral villages with wisdom of ancestors
Rural countryside villages where we slow down
Music, laughter & joy is filled in cityscapes and animals in nature have a peaceful space to hear the hum of crickets.
Multi-family and mixed-use developments are abundant and offer walkable, healthy and easily accessible services.
Spaces are accessible

More parks
• To play
• To listen to the sounds of nature
• More green spaces
• Picnics
• Family gatherings

People know their neighbors a bit better now because they are able to put down roots and share the [?] as each other. This means people know their neighbors where better [?]. Most people are bilingual now.

In this process, humans have forgotten many things: the look of places blanketed in concrete, skyscrapers and single family homes, 2 car garages, hospital and carceral facilities and school shootings. Descendents of today’s resource hoarders have forgotten why they ever wanted to hoard.
Where human habitations are visible, they are communal like the kauhale or marae of the communities of the pacific.
We know our neighbors and that word is constantly expanding for us

A place that we often gather is our market places.  Every neighborhood has a market place - sometimes with multiple floors, almost always with open park spaces for booths where children and adults sell and share things.  There is a community kitchen and plenty of space for people to eat together.  Inside, the walls are lined with baskets and baskets of fresh produce from the nearby farms.  There is a flower stand with buckets of wild flowers harvested by the elementary school from the meadow on the top of the hill.  The shelves are full of jams, local honey, dried seaweed, acorn flour, teff, masa, and corn husks.  We go to the market often to get groceries but also just to see each other.

There isn’t a separation between where we live and nature.  Nature is everywhere - our neighborhoods are green with trees and trails, not just roads for vehicles like trolleys and bikes.  We grow food and tend animals in our community gardens and backyards.

Walking at night in a city without crime. Parks free of homeless people and clean. Affordable and safe housing. Quality schools for everyone. Free programs like computer classes, English, and Zumba. Clean streets. Jobs for everyone.
Original of Translation: Caminar por la noche en una ciudad sin delincuencia. Parques libres de vagabundos y limpos. Rentas accesibles y seguras. Escuelas de calidad para todos. Programas como computacion, ingles, zumba, gratis. Calles limpias. Empleos para todos

Content: I would like us to have clean and safe streets. That there wouldn’t be so much junk food. That in the parks there wouldn’t be people drinking or trash

Being able to take the children to the park and not be afraid to walk on clean and safe streets. Lower rent, cleaner and safer schools. More areas with vegetation. Fewer people living on the streets. More security and fewer robberies.
Our streets clean and safe, so we can play in the gardens where we plant and harvest our fruits and vegetables
Clean streets, no violence in our city. No people living on the streets.

But truth be told, it is difficult to identify the line between built and natural spaces, as peopleʻs built creations so beautifully and effectively resemble nature, and natureʻs genius. These naturally inspired creations, leverage, activate, and catalyze natural processes that create the kind of universally accessible, reproducible and sharable abundance that our money-based economy of the past struggled to.
Aloha in the streets!

In the built environment, space is being used, lived in — no more empty condos owned by absent foreign investors. The ancient concept of “village” has re-emerged as neighborhoods return to places of deep caring for each other. Returning to the village, we remembered each other. We remembered where we are from.

Playgrounds are being used. There are long “lines” if you can call them that, the playgrounds attract a neurodiverse community, so people sharing and taking turns on play structures don’t always take the form of lines but no one's behavior is considered mental illness. Cultivating and honoring this neurodiversity and the talent that accompanies it has led to an explosion of visual arts, practiced widely and skillfully, with unimaginable expressiveness.

There are architectural relics from 2025 that were McMansions, 5000 sq ft single family homes repurposed into intentional learning communities where people live there with folks who hold wisdom around what they want to learn and grow. People can move freely through these communities and learn from the wisdom holders and teachers .

Solar power. Smaller communities centered on community amenities. Buildings in the round.  Multi-family houses centered around leadership centers, shared working and gathering spaces. Airborne vehicles that can take you to other communities. Plant based diets. Both individual hydroponic gardens and community gardens.
Museum of absurd and inhumane.
Prisons are torn down and turned into community scenters that provide mentoring resources.

Services and products are high quality. And we enjoy good physical spaces. There is no longer such a thing as private beaches, private golf courses, private schools, private hospitals, or gated communities. It now seems crazy that they ever did.

Neighbors will talk to one another.  They will feel accountable to one another.  When people walk dawn the street, you can expect to get harassed (in a good way) by the old ladies.  They’ll be hustling the kids around, checking on parents, and giving old men lots of good trouble.
People who live in small towns will recognize they have everything they need.  They will walk tall and with purpose.

Date/Circle Name: 10/30/25 Kailua, HI Polynesian Club, Le Jardin Academy
Content: A thriving future will have a good, eco-friendly infrastructure where humans all take care of their environment to help reverse the effects of pollution. Cities are less grey and no longer filled with smoke. Neon signs are gone, no one can imagine dirty roads or trash. Streams under bridges run clear.
Green space to be grounded in more widely available
In a sort of townsquare, there are community booths with what was grown, shared, traded

Neighborhoods where empathy is the infrastructure - it’s flowing through every elder and every child, every garden, every living and sentient being, every silence and every open heart and hand across the world.

In this neighborhood, the day begins slowly. Morning light stretches across all the front porches, the garden beds and rooftops. Elders sit close with their families - laughing. The elders speak their wisdom and stories are like medicine for the youngsters. As you walk through the neighborhood everyone is acknowledged. There is also silence, but it’s spacious and allows everyone to really listen to their surroundings, to mother earth, to the birds to the crawling of the bugs.

In East Boston there are more trees than there are today. We have repurposed parking lots and condominiums for community gardens. There is a place for people from all generations to gather in a community meeting spot where we have joy – like dances in El Salvador, cultural events of joy and sharing space. The old buildings are there but also smaller eco-friendly homes, with gardens and botanicals growing all over them. Green spaces in every nook and cranny. Nests and birds doing their thing everywhere. Chelsea Creek is clean and people are swimming in it. There are no longer any cargo ships so it’s safe to paddle and canoe there.
Solar Punk - Living with nature. Having vernacular architecture, community care, and an economy based on people’s wellbeing. Free libraries, food stands – take what you want, leave what you can.
Commons – We value the commons around healing, collective community support and care. Food, learning, art/beauty, shelter/home are the categories that are freely and accessible in the commons.
Buildings fit into the surroundings.  They are there…but you can’t see them very easily.

Communities are connected by mass transit that is modern, clean, safe, and sustainable. Close-knit & walkable communities – we know our neighbors and care for each other. Streets are accessible and navigable for all. Our roads will not be car centered. We can walk and bike. Our necessities are nearby. Our sidewalks are smooth and buildings have ramps that make sense.

The village is set up in a circle, with the elders and family housing on the perimeter. Transitional youth housing is one layer in, including housing for foster children. Inside of that layer is housing for Veterans. There is trees and a large greenbelt around the whole property. The middle holds a Resource Center that includes a pantry and place for clothing. There is a rec room and next door is the urgent care and police substation. Across the way is a barbershop and the DBH (sic) and the VA support center. In the very center of the community is the basketball court, pickleball court, and playground. There also bodies of water and a pool for everyone.
We live in smaller scale communities with attention to the roles we play and what it takes to center community-living. Many places have weekly town parties!
Neighbors come out to sing lullabies to each other to close the day towards rest and prepare themselves for tomorrow
The air is perfumed with the fragrance of fruit trees and neighborhood Block party meals
As the sunset had just eclipsed and the moon was rising, neighbors come out to sing lullabies to each other to close the day and prepare themselves for tomorrow.
Children and neighbors of many languages growing up on the same block, sharing meals, having each other's backs when times are tough.
Neighbors look out for one another, help meet needs. Kids play in each other’s yards or at the nearby park. Laughing and talking.

Green space everywhere. Every home has a dedicated space for a small herb garden even if its just a planter box in a window sill. Everyone is able to access (walkable distance) a community garden that has seasonal fruits and veggies. Garden planted with intention. Roofs and walls of buildings built with natural, local materials that can also host plants (and pollinators). Reusing materials. Outsourcing is minimized or non-existent.
Downtowns are green with pops of color and have so much nature. No one needs to "get away."

Date/Circle Name: 8/18/26 A New Way of Life Los Angeles
Content: Most buildings last hundreds of years so the future homes will have old and new technology.

Neighborhood: people living in the same area, helping each other and sharing local spaces. Local parks bring people together in the same shared space. People use the park for recreation, relationships and socializing.

Society advances to the point where we don’t live on the ground level anymore. Cities turn into rural areas. Cities are a think of the past. Society is elevated to the point where this no longer a floor level.

All this happens in very green cities. Where generations grow up in neighborhoods where everyone has the opportunity to thrive, contribute and feel a sense of belonging. When a building project is needed or proposed, the neighborhood of the project takes the lead and co-creates the design and has the final decision. Vacation homes and AirBnBs are changed into homes for the unhoused. No one is without a home, food is in abundance, everyone is clothed.
Can you hear it? Of course you can: the sounds of birds in the air are cacophonous, waking the whole neighborhood.

Plants are nourishment and medicine as planter boxes and edible gardens line the streets. Vertical living incorporates nature and native species and landscapes in both preserved and newly built communities. Proximity to neighbors is not crowding – communities clusters provide access to food resources, integrated health and preventative care at all ages. Self-resilience means farm land for the unhoused and no more people living on the street.
Every city has a community garden, and in Concord, vacant lots were turned into a community space.
Original of Translation: Cada barrio tiene un concilio con jóvenes y mayores que guía la comunidad y tiene un representante en el concilio grande de la ciudad.

Content: People can walk to their jobs because they are located nearby in their neighborhoods.
Original of Translation: La gente puede caminar a sus trabajos porque les queda cerca en sus vecindarios.
